implementation_statement: The vendors provide account functions; the owner creates and removes accounts. SYS-01 has two accounts: the owner (administrator) and the irrigation dealer's technician (full irrigation control since 2024). Gaps: the dealer account has never been reviewed and stays on all year; the laptop has one administrator account shared with family members; no periodic account review.
evidence: SYS-01 user list exported 2026-07-15; laptop user settings

implementation_statement: SYS-01 enforces its roles (administrator, irrigation technician, viewer). Only the administrator and irrigation technician roles can start, stop, or schedule irrigation. The owner assigns the roles.
evidence: SYS-01 role settings; vendor SOC 2 report (P09)

implementation_statement: Gaps: the dealer's technician account can change any schedule and setpoint at both sites although the dealer only needs read access between service visits; family members use the laptop with administrator rights. Plan: viewer role for the dealer except during an owner-approved service window; separate standard user accounts on the laptop (2026-09-30).
evidence: SYS-01 role settings; laptop user settings

implementation_statement: All remote control of the pump and pivot goes through SYS-01 over the vendor's connection; no device has an inbound port open to the internet (router check 2026-07-16). Gaps: the dealer's remote control rights are always on with no usage rules, and the vendor's support access setting is on permanently. The dealer agreement has no security terms.
evidence: SYS-01 user list and support access setting; router port check

implementation_statement: Home Wi-Fi uses WPA2 with a passphrase. Gap: the farm-stand customer Wi-Fi password is posted at the stand and the customer network is the same network as the laptop and the pump controller's Wi-Fi bridge. Plan: guest network isolation and a separate network for the pump house (2026-11-15).
evidence: Router settings 2026-07-16

implementation_statement: The owner has learned security only from vendor videos. The owner will complete a free small-business cybersecurity course and subscribe to monthly reminders by 2026-11-30, and will brief family members who use the laptop.
evidence: Course certificate (planned)

implementation_statement: SYS-01 keeps an activity log of sign-ins and irrigation commands, and the email and booking platforms keep sign-in history; nobody has reviewed them. Starting 2026-10, the owner reviews all three on the first Monday of each month, and weekly in freeze season, and notes the review in the security log.
evidence: SYS-01 activity log screen viewed 2026-07-15; review log (planned)

implementation_statement: The owner knows the devices, but there was no written list before this plan. Section 9 of the SSP and POL-01 Appendix A now list each system and device; firmware versions and default-password status of the OT devices still need to be recorded.
evidence: SSP section 9; POL-01 Appendix A

implementation_statement: The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gaps: the written freeze-night procedure, the mutual-aid arrangement with a neighbor, the standalone freeze alarm, and the sealed recovery codes are not in place yet (due 2026-11-30).

Owner responsibility: the laptop and the cloud files have no backup or version history, SYS-01 has never been exported, and the qualified exemption sales records exist only in SYS-09 and SYS-10.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report (P09); file account settings

evidence: SYS-01 user list

implementation_statement: MFA is on for email (text message codes), online banking, and the accounting SaaS. Gap: the owner's SYS-01 administrator account, which can start and stop irrigation, and the booking platform admin account use a password only although both offer MFA. Owner turns MFA on with an authenticator app by 2026-09-15.
evidence: Account security pages; P07 sign-in test

implementation_statement: Gaps: the same password is used on SYS-01 and the booking platform; every farm password is saved in the shared laptop browser; the router admin password is the factory default; the pump controller's local web page uses the manufacturer's default password (found in P07 testing). Plan: password manager with unique passphrases; change all default passwords (2026-09-15).
evidence: P07 IA-5 tests; router and pump controller login pages

implementation_statement: The ransomware and account takeover runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-08-31 with a contact list. Gap: contacts not yet printed, the plan not yet walked through, and the neighbor not yet briefed (due 2026-11-30).
evidence: P08 runbook

implementation_statement: The pump house and equipment barn are padlocked; the pivot panel at River Field has a locked cabinet; the laptop stays in the home office.
evidence: Walkthrough 2026-07-14

implementation_statement: First risk assessment completed 2026-07-17 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed each July and after a major change.
evidence: P01 risk register

implementation_statement: The FMIS vendor's SOC 2 report was obtained and reviewed (P09). Gaps: no security terms with the irrigation dealer; the AI yield vendor (SYS-08) uses click-through terms that let it use farm data; no vendor list; vendors holding personal information (booking platform, accounting SaaS) have not been asked who receives their breach notices.
evidence: Vendor terms; P09 review

implementation_statement: The router's firewall blocks inbound connections and no port is forwarded (checked 2026-07-16). The pivot panel uses the vendor's cellular connection, outside the home network. Gap: one flat network for customer Wi-Fi, the laptop, and the pump controller. Plan: separate networks with no traffic from the guest network to the farm network (2026-11-15).
evidence: Router settings; network walkthrough

provider_if_inherited: FMIS vendor; booking platform vendor; card processor
implementation_statement: SYS-01 web and app traffic, the booking platform, and the card reader use encrypted connections (TLS; card data encrypted at the reader). The vendor states that pivot panel commands travel over an encrypted channel. Owner responsibility: no farm logins over the farm-stand customer Wi-Fi.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; browser connection check

implementation_statement: The laptop has full-disk encryption; the phone and tablet are encrypted by their passcodes; the SaaS vendors encrypt data at rest (SYS-01 confirmed in its SOC 2 report).
evidence: Device encryption status (P07); vendor SOC 2 report

implementation_statement: The SaaS vendors patch their platforms. Automatic updates are on for the laptop, phone, and tablet. Gaps: the router firmware has never been updated, and the pump controller and pivot panel firmware have not been checked since installation in 2024.
evidence: Update history; router and controller firmware pages

implementation_statement: The laptop's built-in antivirus runs real-time scanning with automatic updates. Owner responsibility: keep it on, act on alerts, and scan USB sticks from the tractor display and drone before opening files.
evidence: Antivirus status page (P07 test)
